en.html:
Hachimangu may be called the center of Kamakura. Geographically, historically, politically: on all three counts.

In Imperial Year 1723 (1063 by the foreign calendar), Yoriyoshi Minamoto, second head of the Seiwa-line Kawachi Genji, took his clan god Hachiman and enshrined him at Tsurugaoka, which was his own territory. About one hundred years later, his descendant Yoritomo opened the warrior capital Kamakura with Hachimangu in the middle.

Eight hundred years have passed since, and Kamakura's Hachimangu has stood as guardian deity of the Genji—no, of the warrior class as a whole. The Rokuhara clan, who today call themselves heads of the Genji, show it extraordinary devotion.

A regular visit several times a year is not enough for them. For every happy occasion and every unhappy one, a ceremony is held. Such an undertaking cannot help carrying the color of political publicity, so it grows grand, automatically. Frequent rebuilding and lavish decoration probably have the same reason. Beauty on the building is politics on the building.

And one more decoration of that type, you could say, is the person who was invited all the way from the capital in Kyoto and received in the inner hall.

Deep in the Hachimangu grounds stands one small, quiet hall... It is said that the Maidono which now stands near the center, was once on this very spot. Hence its second name, Inner Maidono.

The resident of the small hall takes his title from that tradition.

八幡宮は鎌倉の中心にあるといえる。
　地理的にも、歴史的にも、政治的にも。

　国紀一七二三（外暦一〇六三）年、清和系河内源氏
二代目棟梁にあたる源頼義が氏神たる八幡神を所領で
あった鶴岡に祀り――およそ百年後、彼の後裔頼朝は
八幡宮を中心に武家の都・鎌倉を開く。

　爾来八百年、鎌倉の八幡宮は源氏の守護神……否、
武士の守護神として在った。
　現代において源氏棟梁を称する六波羅一門も、並々
ならぬ崇敬を寄せている。

　年数回の定例参拝を行うのみならず、慶事凶事の折
につけ祭儀を催した。
　その種の事業は政治宣伝の色合いを帯びずにはいら
れない。勢い盛大なものになる。

　頻繁に改築を行い、豪奢な装いを調えることも理由
は同じだろう。美観上の装飾はつまり政治上の装飾。
　――言うなれば、その一つなのだ。はるばる京の都
から招かれ、奥殿へ迎えられたかの人物も。

　八幡宮境内の深部にひっそりと建つ小殿……
　現在は中央付近にある<ruby>舞殿<rt>まいどの</rt></ruby>が、かつてはその場所に
あったと伝えられる。故に一名、奥舞殿。

　小殿の主が称する名はその伝承に由来した。

en.html:
Maidono-no-miya Haruhiro Shinno.

Youngest son of the late Emperor. In the line of succession he stands second, after Crown Prince Motohiro.

That he was installed as betto, the chief of Hachimangu's rites, proves—nothing else it can possibly prove—the depth of Rokuhara's faith and loyalty to the throne. Or so it was decided. On the surface.

In reality: a declaration of Rokuhara's authority, that it can move even the Imperial House as it pleases. And—nothing more than a hostage. Kyoto's human sacrifice to Rokuhara.

The shadow wavering beyond the bamboo blind was that kind of existence.

　先帝の末子にあたり、皇位継承順位では基煕皇太子
に次ぐ第二位に位置する。

　彼が八幡宮の祭祀長職たる別当として奉じられた事
は、まさしく六波羅の信仰心と勤皇精神の厚かりしを
顕すものに他ならない。
　……ということに、されていた。表向きは。

　実際のところ。
　皇室をも自在に動かし得るという六波羅の権威表明
であり、そして――人質に過ぎない。
　京都が六波羅に差し出した人身御供。

　御簾の向こうにゆらめく影は、そうした存在だった。

To be honest, I wished to be excused. If I refused, probably he would not force me.

Silver Star is, after all, my private matter. No matter what others think, that does not shake. So the prince's sense of being "far away" is, if anything, desirable. I have no need to shorten it.

I begin from the beginning, in order, keeping emotion out of my words as far as possible.

さよ 「赤い糸の導きというものでございましょう」
香奈枝 「きゃっ。もうばあやったら、いやなひと」
景明 「……」
舞殿宮 「なんや、随分仲良しさんやないか。 　隅に置けんな、景明くん」
署長 「宮殿下？」

署長 「……は。 　なるほど」
舞殿宮 「ＧＨＱがそういうのを寄越してくれるって 話は前からあったやろう？ 　その人選がやっと決まって、このお二人が 来たってことみたいやわ」

香奈枝 「当方の不手際で宮殿下には不自由をお掛け してしまいました。 　申し訳ございません」

香奈枝 「わたくしの職務は司令部を代表して宮殿下 のお側に仕え、諸事に便宜を図ること。 　きっとお役に立ちましょう。殿下におかれ ては心置きなく、何なりとお命じ下さいまし」
舞殿宮 「……そうですか。 　それは有り難いお話や。なぁ、署長？」
署長 「は。 　まったく、良い人が来てくれたものです」

舞殿宮"............"
Chief"............"
Kanae"Of the past, and of the future. ...Yes. The future."
Kanae"At present, interference in this country's internal affairs: practically none. The Occupation Army occupies, and there its activity ends. Withdrawal soon, people are even saying..."
Kanae"Of course, withdrawal is not on the cards. As all of you know very well."
Kageaki"..."
Kanae"Six years ago—the League Army accepted Rokuhara's surrender, on condition that the shogunate govern Yamato, and the Great War ended."
Kanae"Only, this was not the ending the League Army had in mind. Let us say Britain plainly. They consider themselves the world's leaders; complete occupation of Yamato in the Far East was not optional for them."
Kanae"To stop the last enemy, the Russian Empire, from expanding any further. Leave Yamato alone, and it may become the exit to the southern seas that Russia longs for, by conquest or by alliance..."
Kanae"Then their worldwide blockade of Russia, built with such success, comes to nothing. All that work, gone. Such a risk they could hardly overlook."
Kanae"...Even so, they agreed to end the war because Rokuhara's peace proposal made war-weariness rise all at once in the League nations, and it could not be held down. Front and rear were probably both exhausted, too."
Kanae"One further difficulty. Force an occupation under those conditions, and how long would the resistance continue? An extremely long time, by the prediction."
Kageaki"...For the Commonwealth, which wants a bridgehead against Russia, that is inconvenient. It would be the same as tossing good bait in front of Russia's mouth—counterproductive in the extreme. Is that it?"
Kanae"Yes, exactly. From those circumstances, the peace of six years ago came about."
Kanae"But of course the Commonwealth—GHQ—has not given up. It is laying stones, so that it can move its army again in Yamato and achieve complete occupation."
Kanae"Rokuhara's tyranny—let it continue, say nothing. That is one such move. They are waiting for hatred of the shogunate to boil over among Yamato's people; then for the world to demand Yamato's liberation."
Kanae"For the right time to light the fuse of a "just war" that no one in the world can point a finger at..."
Kageaki"..."

en.html:
The chief lowers his eyes. Perhaps he judges that what needed drawing out has been drawn out.

The screen hides the prince's face, and I cannot read it. Yet I feel I can see a mouth chewing on something bitter.

Indirect when it looks direct, direct when it looks indirect. Captain Ootori's method would puzzle more than a prince.

She must be doing it deliberately... No. Perhaps she is simply behaving naturally.

Or perhaps she behaves without a thought, while knowing perfectly well what each careless act will produce. A strategy made of no strategy.

...I, too, am being confounded.

What does the prince intend to do...?
